- When sentiment is negative or near-zero over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for such periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 2+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts — increase forecast slightly to reflect mean reversion toward prior range.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights recent highs; apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if recent 5-day average is >10% above 30-day average.  
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat or declining, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slope or apply dampening factor to avoid false momentum.
